entries.ea2bd2c8c408baa5: The bank is pursuing its 7th Medium-Term Management Plan, 'Change & Challenge', covering April 2024 to March 2029. Stating its purpose as 'We will realize a bank that loves the region, always stays close to customers and is most relied upon', the bank announced a revision of the plan in May 2026 in light of changes in the financial and economic environment, and reorganized its priority strategies into four: 'transforming the earnings structure in a world with interest rates', 'strengthening regional financial capabilities through corporate support', 'pursuing efficient management through organizational and DX reform', and 'establishing an efficient and effective governance framework'. Under a capital and business alliance with Plan Do See Co., Ltd., the bank is also working on regional revitalization through, among other things, the development of hospitality businesses in the Hokuriku area and elsewhere, centered on Toyama Prefecture.
entries.ebb85338e807c19d: Headquartered in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture, with 39 outlets including the head office, and based in Toyama and Ishikawa prefectures, where it actively promotes these operations, it positions banking as its core business. Together with leasing operations and credit guarantee operations by consolidated subsidiaries, it provides financial services to customers in the region.
entries.f72b09b9ef62c2e4: The Bank of Toyama,Ltd. is headquartered in Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture, and forms a group with 2 consolidated subsidiaries. Founded in 1954 as Toyama Sangyo Bank, it changed its name to The Bank of Toyama,Ltd. in 1967. Consolidated number of employees is 325 (as of March 31, 2026).
entries.f7c06593f18b33d2: The breakdown of consolidated ordinary income of ¥13,771 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026 is: by segment, ordinary income from external customers of ¥12,010 million for banking, ¥1,743 million for leasing and ¥33 million for others (guarantee operations). By service, ordinary income was ¥5,951 million from securities investment operations, ¥4,517 million from loan operations, ¥1,736 million from leasing operations and ¥1,225 million from service transaction operations. Ordinary income from domestic external customers exceeds 90%, and no specific customer accounts for 10% or more of ordinary income.
